name: plan-medium-council
description: The Medium Council (0.8.4): the middle of three planning chains (plan-mini-council, plan-medium-council, plan-high-council). It runs the planning stages with three proposers (Claude Sonnet 5.5, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM-5.3) and a layered review panel of eight named judges in three layers: layer 1 Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Luna, MiniMax M3.1 Flash; layer 2 GLM-5.3, Mistral Large 4, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash; layer 3 Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol. Each seat carries a persona name in the form title (seat_personas), which is the title of the seat and changes nothing the seat does. Exactly these eight vote, eight judges from six companies (Claude Haiku 5.5 and Claude Opus 5.5 are one company, GPT-6 Luna and GPT-6.1 Sol are one company); DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM-5.3 each both propose and judge, which is why "judging" is "all-roles". Every layer has at least two judges. A layer signs off when all its judges do. Any objection at a lower layer sends the draft to the reviser; a round ends only when layer 3 gives its verdict, a sign-off or an objection. This chain runs the ladder (its ladder key: block 3, visits 3): layer 1 revises in blocks of 3, then layer 2 is asked (up to 3 visits), then layer 3 reads; each layer-3 visit is one top-layer read. It has no round limit: the run ends on agreement, on a stall the top layer holds, at the limit you type (--rounds counts top-layer reads) or when you stop it. When a stall at the top layer, a judge that stays silent after its solo ask, or your own stop ends the work for now, the run is stopped, resumable and NOT agreed, and you choose how to go on: continue, finish at once, finish after one last top-layer read, or revise the draft yourself; the run's spending limit still applies. On a ladder run the plan is never sent up a layer ahead of its turn: each layer is asked when the ladder's order reaches it. The three Claude seats (Claude Sonnet 5.5 as a proposer, Claude Haiku 5.5 and Claude Opus 5.5 as judges) are called through Anthropic's API (provider anthropic) with an Anthropic key, and go through OpenRouter without one; the other eight seats (six models) are called through OpenRouter and need an OpenRouter key. Every OpenRouter seat asks OpenRouter not to route it to the Open Inference provider (provider.ignore). answer_back is on: a judge's own earlier objection is shown back to it, and only that judge can close it. The criteria, skeleton, build, revise and handoff stages need a Claude Code session (provider external): they pause the run (exit 3) until the session answers. Every API seat reasons at high; no Grok, no Kimi. Output caps are the largest reply the harness knows for each model: Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5, Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna 128,000; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 393,216; GLM-5.3 131,072. For MiniMax M3.1 Flash and Mistral Large 4 no published limit was found, so the seat cap is 128,000. Dry run (0.8.4, prices of 2026-11-11, the dry run's assumed sizes): $14.78 expected (3 top-layer reads, the read that signs off counted, each after a climb of about 8 layer-1 passes and 1 layer-2 pass: the average of one measured run) and an upper estimate of $631.91 (7 top-layer reads, an assumption, each with the full ladder below it), about $14.78 plus a Claude subscription. The upper estimate counts the in-pass re-asks (up to 2 per seat) and the solo ask of a silent judge at the review's expected cost, but leaves out answer-back calls, the memory block judge calls read from overseer round 2 on (up to 10000 tokens per call, paid input that neither figure prices) and the larger prompt the top layer reads, so it is not a ceiling: the limit you type is what stops spending. No proposer's cap is below the most the harness will retry its model at, so a proposal cut off at its cap is not asked again with a bigger one. The upper estimate ($631.91) and the expected figure ($14.78) are above the default cap of $12; the cheapest end ($8.83, one overseer round, the dry run's floor) fits under it. On the command line that cap is not a limit for a paid run: it is the figure the dry run compares a chain with. The Claude Desktop bundle's default Spend ceiling of $12 is a hard ceiling nobody can type above, so with that default a run that uses its whole allowance stops at the ceiling (the upper estimate and the expected figure are above it; the cheapest end, $8.83, fits under it). Type a limit above the upper estimate to keep the run from stopping at its limit unless a call outside the plan adds up or the run needs more than the seven assumed top-layer reads; a lower limit, even the expected figure, can stop it there (exit 4, resumable with a higher total). This roster has not run, and none of its mechanisms has been measured. Price your task with `npm run dry` and get an explicit go before any paid run.
summary: Eight judges in three layers. Claude seats on Anthropic's API, the rest on OpenRouter.
